historical_reviews.deepseek: Inventory access is conceptually relevant but broad selection can confuse SMC, SMC-FPGA and UBB-FPGA records and insecure transport undermines evidence identity.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds exact amc_fpga_active resource, component/schema mapping, trusted endpoint, secure credential flow, redaction and audit timestamps.
historical_reviews.related_cases: The preceding SMC controller version and following UBB FPGA version are separate firmware identities with distinct active resources.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Preserves the component boundary rather than treating all FPGA or AMC entries as interchangeable.

original_test_intent: Prove the active FPGA firmware associated with the SMC/AMC component on the intended baseboard matches the approved GPU release bundle.
original_method: Query the exact amc_fpga_active member through an authenticated TLS-verified Redfish session, bind the redacted response to the unique SMC FPGA identity/active state and compare version against the supplied release record.
manual_activity: Engineering/security provides the trusted service and SMC-FPGA release mapping; engineer handles mismatches and owns PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.
required_inputs: Approved BMC/Redfish host, TLS trust and ACL route
Vendor mapping for amc_fpga_active to physical SMC FPGA
Expected active FPGA version and authoritative release bundle
safety_requirements: Use read-only least privilege and exact resource scope
Confirm exactly one expected FPGA member and active state
Stop on trust/auth/schema/identity/version-format or audit error
Exclude secrets and all mutation actions
agent_execution_scope: Perform one authorized exact firmware-inventory GET
Capture status/time and the permitted redacted component fields
Compare active SMC-FPGA version with supplied release baseline
Do not enumerate unnecessarily, disable validation, invoke update/reset or set verdict
engineer_actions: Approve trust/access and amc_fpga component mapping
Resolve identity/version/security anomalies and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The broad untrusted request cannot disambiguate the SMC FPGA from controller or UBB FPGA records and leaks management secrets.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Query exact amc_fpga_active over verified HTTPS with brokered read-only credentials and compare its unique active version to the release bundle.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: SMC FPGA active-member intent, release comparison and source 5/5 timing remain unchanged.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Store only component identity, active flag, version, resource URI, verified BMC fingerprint and release baseline in the review evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes broad insecure access and prevents cross-FPGA confusion.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: SMC controller and UBB FPGA versions remain independent adjacent checkpoints.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: AMC/SMC naming is vendor-specific and must be tied to the physical component map.

project_override_considerations: An alternate secure SMC tool is acceptable only if it unambiguously reports the same active SMC FPGA image and release mapping; flashing is excluded.
expected_evidence: Authorized read-only account role without secret material
Exact amc_fpga_active URI/status/timestamp and redacted fields
Approved release mapping and comparison result
Access audit/security observations and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title and exact amc_fpga_active URI consistently identify SMC FPGA firmware; adjacent component similarity is handled by explicit identity mapping.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Trust, access, component mapping and expected version can be supplied; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Creates an exact, trusted SMC-FPGA active-image comparison and prevents broad inventory or other component versions from producing a false match.
independent_technical_reasoning: FPGA versions can coincide across SMC and UBB while referring to different images, so version equality alone is weak. The Redfish member ID, active state and vendor component map must all agree. Restricting the response also reduces credential/inventory exposure while keeping the firmware assertion complete.
